newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends up after volatile trade amid rumours.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends up after volatile trade amid rumours.

text.p: Share prices were volatile in lively trade and the bourse closed off highs as telecoms major Nokia retreated from earlier strong gains sparked by rumours that it would merge with its rival Ericsson, brokers said.
The HEX general index added 0.77 percent to 2,433.4 points.

Options and futures expiry boosted trading but Nokia occupied centre court, closing up 5.00 at 260.50 after hitting a 265 markka intra-session peak. Volume in Nokia was a massive 450 million markka, half of total trade.
Analysts said the merger rumours were ill-informed but some added there were also fundamental grounds for Nokia to rise.

The dollar's strength and early gains in U.S. treasuries following a decline in the U.S. trade deficit in October helped shares in the afternoon, leaving some scope for further gains on Friday if bonds stay strong, brokers said.
Forest industry stocks were supported by the firm dollar and the sector's gains in the U.S. but overall trade was thin.
However, dealings in Europe's largest paper maker UPM-Kymmene was active and the share closed flat at 94.00 markka after almost 60 million markka trade.
Amer see-sawed but ended in positive territory after opening weak after it said in a newsletter that restructuring of the Wilson golf business would take time. It closed at 90.50, up 0.80 markka.
